title: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
thread:
**Issue #2013 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2013: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 40362255453](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40362255453) on `bot/issue-1996` (`edc1e52`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [db (deploy image crates)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40362255453/job/121711516226) | 7m 55s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom: most splits only need a longer matrix list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)`, or `rust (test <group>)`, whose crate groups split further, a crate's test binaries apart with `--lib`/`--test <name>`); for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`. Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`. Make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere (the e2e `WEIGHTS`, a slow test made faster or split across files), and when the split needs `ci.yml`'s matrix, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40365099265)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`db (deploy image crates)` took 7m55s on #1996's pull request, which changed only `crates/server`. That job compiles the engine, the cards, the AI and the server's library in one Dockerfile stage (`COPY crates ./crates`), so it starts over whenever anything under `crates/` changes. Done means:

- The `crates` stage is split in two. A new `game` stage builds the engine, the cards and the AI. The `crates` stage then builds only the server's library on top of it.
- The image and its binary stay byte for byte the same.
- `rehearse.sh` accepts `REHEARSAL_STAGE=game`, and unit tests hold all of this.
- A person makes the `ci.yml` half: a `db-deploy-game` job and one cache scope per stage. The scopes are #1787's lines, which were never applied. The bot may not edit `.github/`.

The planner measured on this 4-core runner (Docker 28, buildx 0.38):

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| plain `docker build`, the compile alone | crates 96 s | game 54 s, then server library 51 s |
| container builder, local cache per stage, crates job | 148 s (exports 147 MB of new layers) | 90 s (exports about 55 MB) |
| game job after a server-only change | n/a | 26 s, every step cached |
| binary sha256 | `2b6cc3a3…2fd8804` | identical |

CI's extra five minutes or so beyond this are cache transfer, which cannot be measured here.

## Files to touch

| Path | New/change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/Dockerfile` | change | Header paragraph. New `game` stage. `crates` stage copies only `crates/server`. |
| `crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh` | change | Header comment. `game` added to the two `case "$STAGE"` lists and to the FAIL message. |
| `apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts` | change | Header comment. Two new tests. The refusal test's message. The Dockerfile-order test. |

Do not touch:
- `.github/` (the `ci.yml` part is a person's, under Open questions).
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh`: the Dockerfile and `tests/deploy/*` are already on its `web` and `db_deploy` lines.
- `render.yaml`, any crate's `src/` or `Cargo.toml`, `spec/`, `BUILD.md`, `crates/cards/patches/`.

No spec section or ruling governs this. It is CI only. There is no patch fragment, because no catalog or card changes (#1565 and #1787 had none).

## Steps

1. **`crates/server/Dockerfile`, header lines 10–14.** Replace the text from `# Five stages build` through `# on every change, in two stages so that CI can build them in two jobs. The image is the` with exactly the block below. Line 15, `# last stage, a slim Debian…`, follows it unchanged.
   ```
   # Six stages build `jackioh-server` in release, cargo-chef's way: the tool (`chef`), the recipe
   # (`planner`), the dependencies (`deps`), the engine, the cards and the AI (`game`), the server's
   # library (`crates`), then the server's binary (`build`). The dependencies (some 260 crates) sit in a
   # layer of their own that a change to the sources alone does not rebuild, and the engine, the cards
   # and the AI in one that a change to the server alone does not; the server's library and the
   # thin-LTO link are compiled on every change, each stage on its own so that CI can build each in a
   # job of its own. The image is the
   ```

2. **Same file, the `crates` stage (lines 68–79).** That is the comment starting `# The workspace's crates: the real manifests and sources over the skeleton,` through `RUN cargo build --release --locked -p jackioh-server --lib`. Replace all of it with exactly:
   ```
   # The crates the server builds on, the engine, the cards and the AI: the real manifests and their
   # sources over the skeleton, built by the server's own command below (so with its features) while
   # the server is still the skeleton's empty crate. Only these three of crates/ are copied, so this
   # layer is rebuilt only when they, a manifest or the lock file change: a change to the server alone,
   # or to crates/tools, crates/luau or crates/wasm, reuses it (#2013). A crate the server comes to
   # build on needs a COPY line here, or the server's build below fails on its empty skeleton.
   # `cargo clean -p jackioh-server` then drops what the empty server left in target/, as `cargo chef
   # cook` drops the skeleton's compiled crates: the server's sources copied below keep the build
   # context's times, older than this build, so cargo would take the empty build script for fresh
   # and the library would not compile (JACKIOH_RULES_FINGERPRINT not defined). A stage of its own, so
   # CI can build it and write it to the layer cache in a job of its own
   # (crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh's REHEARSAL_STAGE=game): on 4 cores this compile took 54 s.
   FROM deps AS game
   COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock ./
   COPY crates/engine ./crates/engine
   COPY crates/cards ./crates/cards
   COPY crates/ai ./crates/ai
   RUN cargo build --release --locked -p jackioh-server --lib \
    && cargo clean --release --locked -p jackioh-server

   # The server's library on the crates above: its sources, and nothing above compiled again. `--lib`
   # leaves out only the server's binary, whose thin-LTO link generates the whole program's machine
   # code; the features and the profile are the same, so the build below compiles the binary alone and
   # reuses everything here, and the binary is byte for byte the one a single stage builds. target/
   # stays in this layer for it. A stage of its own, so CI can build it and write it to the layer cache
   # in a job of its own before the rehearsal (crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh's
   # REHEARSAL_STAGE=crates, #1223, #2013): on 4 cores this compile took 51 s and the binary's 122 s.
   FROM game AS crates
   COPY crates/server ./crates/server
   RUN cargo build --release --locked -p jackioh-server --lib
   ```
   Change nothing else in the file; the planner's `COPY crates ./crates` stays. The `cargo clean` line is required: without it the planner's trial failed in the `crates` stage with "environment variable `JACKIOH_RULES_FINGERPRINT` not defined at compile time".

3. **`crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh`, lines 38–45.** Replace the text from `# REHEARSAL_STAGE=deps stops after building` through `# and its thin-LTO link.` with:
   ```
   # REHEARSAL_STAGE=deps stops after building the Dockerfile's `deps` stage (the image's
   # dependencies, `cargo chef cook`), REHEARSAL_STAGE=game after its `game` stage (the engine, the
   # cards and the AI, compiled on them) and REHEARSAL_STAGE=crates after its `crates` stage (the
   # server's library, compiled on those), with the cache flags below: no database, no image, no boot.
   # REHEARSAL_DEPS_ONLY=1 is REHEARSAL_STAGE=deps. CI builds each stage in a job of its own before the
   # rehearsal (#653, #1223, #2013: db-deploy-deps, db-deploy-game, then db-deploy-crates), so a change
   # to a manifest or Cargo.lock, which recompiles every dependency, is paid in the first, the engine,
   # the cards and the AI in the second, the server's library in the third, and the rehearsal's own
   # build compiles only the server's binary and its thin-LTO link.
   ```

4. **Same file, lines 57–58.** Change `# with REHEARSAL_LOAD_IMAGE, and neither image flag applies to the deps or crates stages (those` / `# builds tag no image).` to `# with REHEARSAL_LOAD_IMAGE, and neither image flag applies to the deps, game or crates stages` / `# (those builds tag no image).`

5. **Same file, the stage checks.**
   - Line 96: `  "" | deps | crates | image) ;;` becomes `  "" | deps | game | crates | image) ;;`.
   - Line 97: the message becomes `FAIL: REHEARSAL_STAGE is deps, game, crates or image, not $STAGE`.
   - Line 112: `  deps | crates)` becomes `  deps | game | crates)`.

   Leave the build block alone. It already passes `--target "$STAGE"` for any stage but `image`, and it prints `--- the $STAGE stage is built and cached …`.

6. **`apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`, line 2.** Change `` (`deps`, then `crates`) `` to `` (`deps`, `game`, then `crates`) ``.

7. **Same file, new tests.** Add both right after the test `"builds only the deps stage with plain docker build when no cache is given"`:
   ```ts
   it("builds only the game stage through the cache and starts no container", () => {
     const { status, stdout, calls } = rehearse({
       REHEARSAL_STAGE: "game",
       REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: "type=gha,scope=t",
       REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: "type=gha,mode=max,scope=t",
     });
     const [build] = builds(calls);
     expect(status).toBe(0);
     expect(builds(calls)).toHaveLength(1);
     expect(build).toMatch(/^buildx build --target game /);
     expect(build).toContain("--cache-from type=gha,scope=t");
     expect(build).toContain("--cache-to type=gha,mode=max,scope=t");
     expect(build).not.toContain("--load");
     expect(build).not.toContain(" -t ");
     expect(calls.filter((call) => call.startsWith("run "))).toEqual([]);
     expect(stdout).toContain("the game stage is built and cached");
   });

   it("refuses an image flag with the game stage, before any docker call", () => {
     const { status, stderr, calls } = rehearse({ REHEARSAL_STAGE: "game", REHEARSAL_SAVE_IMAGE: "/tmp/deploy-image.tgz" });
     expect(status).not.toBe(0);
     expect(stderr).toContain("need the built image, not the game stage");
     expect(calls).toEqual([]);
   });
   ```

8. **Same file, the refusal test.** Retitle `"refuses a REHEARSAL_STAGE that is neither deps, crates nor image, before any docker call"` to `"refuses a REHEARSAL_STAGE that is neither deps, game, crates nor image, before any docker call"`. Its `toContain` becomes `"REHEARSAL_STAGE is deps, game, crates or image, not build"`.

9. **Same file, the last test.** Replace the whole `it("keeps the cook in a deps stage, …")` with:
   ```ts
   it("keeps the cook in a deps stage, the engine, cards and AI in a game stage on it, the server's library in a crates stage on that, and the binary last", () => {
     const dockerfile = readFileSync(DOCKERFILE, "utf8");
     const at = [
       "\nFROM chef AS deps\n",
       "\nRUN cargo chef cook ",
       "\nFROM deps AS game\n",
       "\nRUN cargo build --release --locked -p jackioh-server --lib \\\n && cargo clean --release --locked -p jackioh-server\n",
       "\nFROM game AS crates\n",
       "\nCOPY crates/server ./crates/server\n",
       "\nRUN cargo build --release --locked -p jackioh-server --lib\n",
       "\nFROM crates AS build\n",
       "\nRUN cargo build --release --locked -p jackioh-server \\\n",
     ].map((needle) => dockerfile.indexOf(needle));
     for (const index of at) expect(index).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
     expect(at).toEqual([...at].sort((a, b) => a - b));
     expect(new Set(at).size).toBe(at.length);
     const stage = (from: number): string => dockerfile.slice(from, dockerfile.indexOf("\nFROM ", from + 1));
     const copied = (text: string): string[] => [...text.matchAll(/^COPY (crates\/\S+) \.\/\1$/gm)].map((match) => match[1] ?? "");
     const game = stage(at[2] ?? -1);
     const crates = stage(at[4] ?? -1);
     expect(copied(game)).toEqual(["crates/engine", "crates/cards", "crates/ai"]);
     expect(copied(crates)).toEqual(["crates/server"]);
     expect(game).not.toContain("\nCOPY crates ./crates\n");
     expect(crates).not.toContain("\nCOPY crates ./crates\n");
     expect(stage(at[7] ?? -1)).not.toContain("\nCOPY ");
   });
   ```
   The `?? -1` and `?? ""` are there for the tsconfig's `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Keep the regex's `m` flag: back-to-back `COPY` lines share one newline.

## Tests

`apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`:
- `builds only the game stage through the cache and starts no container`: one `buildx build --target game` with the cache flags, no `--load`, no `-t`, no `run`. It fails on today's script, which exits 1.
- `refuses an image flag with the game stage, before any docker call`: non-zero exit, the image-flag message, no docker call. Today's script fails it with the wrong message. Without step 5's line-112 change it would exit 0.
- `refuses a REHEARSAL_STAGE that is neither deps, game, crates nor image, before any docker call`: the new message.
- `keeps the cook in a deps stage, the engine, cards and AI in a game stage on it, …`: stage order, the `cargo clean`, the exact COPY lines, no whole-`crates/` copy after the planner, no COPY in `build`.
- The other existing tests still pass unchanged.

Commands, from the repository root:
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`. Its `pretest` builds the WASM module, which the suite's setup imports.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`
- `sh -n crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh`
- When `docker` is available (about 8 minutes cold):
  - `REHEARSAL_STAGE=game sh crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh` exits 0.
  - `REHEARSAL_STAGE=crates sh crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh` exits 0, and its log shows `Compiling jackioh-server` and no other `Compiling jackioh-`.
  - `docker build --target build -t split-check -f crates/server/Dockerfile .`, then `git show origin/main:crates/server/Dockerfile > /tmp/Dockerfile.main`, then `docker build --target build -t main-check -f /tmp/Dockerfile.main .`.
  - `docker run --rm split-check sha256sum /jackioh-server` and the same for `main-check` must print the same hash.
  - Report what you ran. Do not claim the Docker checks if Docker was missing.

## Done when

- [ ] Steps 1–9 are in place, and nothing else changed in those files.
- [ ] `deploy-rehearsal.test.ts` passes in full, and the web typecheck and eslint are clean on it.
- [ ] `sh -n` passes on `rehearse.sh`. The Docker checks, if run, show the same hash.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests.
- [ ] The final report quotes the `ci.yml` changes under Open questions and asks a person to apply them after this merges.

## Risks

- **Render, and super.yml's full rehearsal.** Both build the whole Dockerfile in one plain `docker build`, which is where the mtime trap bites. The planner ran exactly that with this Dockerfile: exit 0, and a binary identical to today's. Keep the `cargo clean` line; step 9's test pins it.
- **A new crate in the server's graph.** It would build as chef's empty skeleton and fail loudly. Any new path dependency changes `Cargo.lock`, which turns on `db_deploy`, so CI catches it. The Dockerfile comment says so.
- **Order of landing.** Until `ci.yml` changes, the current `db-deploy-crates` (`REHEARSAL_STAGE=crates`) builds `game` and `crates` in one job. That works, about 9 s slower locally. The new `db-deploy-game` job must land after this pull request, because today's `rehearse.sh` refuses `game`.
- **First runs.** The new layer keys and scopes start empty, so `game` and `crates` compile once more.

## Open questions

1. **A person must apply this to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after this merges.**
   - (a) Insert this job between `db-deploy-deps` and `db-deploy-crates`:
     ```yaml
     db-deploy-game:
       name: db (deploy image game)
       needs: [changes, db-deploy-deps]
       if: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.full == 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.db_deploy == 'true' }}
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       timeout-minutes: 15
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
         - uses: crazy-max/ghaction-github-runtime@v3
         - name: the image's game stage
           env:
             REHEARSAL_STAGE: game
             REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: "type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal-game"
             REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: type=gha,mode=max,scope=deploy-rehearsal-game
           run: sh crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh
     ```
   - (b) In `db-deploy-crates`, set `needs: [changes, db-deploy-game]` and:
     ```yaml
     REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: "type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal-game type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal-crates"
     REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: type=gha,mode=max,scope=deploy-rehearsal-crates
     ```
   - (c) In `db-deploy-image`, set:
     ```yaml
     REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: "type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal-game type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal-crates type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal-image"
     REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: ${{ (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/staging') && 'type=gha,mode=max,scope=deploy-rehearsal-image' || '' }}
     ```
   - (d) In `db`:
     - add `db-deploy-game` to `needs`, after `db-deploy-deps`;
     - add `GAME: ${{ needs.db-deploy-game.result }}` to its env;
     - add `deploy-game=$GAME` to its `echo`;
     - add `test "$GAME" = success` after `test "$DEPS" = success`.
   - (e) In the comment above `db-deploy-deps`, name `db-deploy-game` (`game`: the engine, the cards and the AI) between deps and crates. Say that each job writes a scope of its own and reads the earlier stages' scopes (#1787, #2013).

   `deploy-rehearsal` stays the deps job's scope, so the cached dependency layer is still found. Branch protection is unchanged: only `db` is required.
2. **If `db (deploy image crates)` still runs past five minutes after that**, its step log will show whether the cache import or the export is the cost. The compile is under 100 s of it. The planner could not measure GitHub's cache service from here. A person picks the next lever: `compression=zstd` on the `REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO` values, a registry cache, or moving the per-PR image build to `super.yml`.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
````

## Goal

`db (deploy image crates)` took 7m55s on #1996's pull request, which changed only `crates/server`. That job compiles the engine, the cards, the AI and the server's library in one Dockerfile stage (`COPY crates ./crates`), so it starts over whenever anything under `crates/` changes. Done means:

- The `crates` stage is split in two. A new `game` stage builds the engine, the cards and the AI. The `crates` stage then builds only the server's library on top of it.

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
